Timeline::from_epoch_seconds¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

static Timeline Timeline::from_epoch_seconds(
    const Series& epoch_seconds,
    std::string_view tz_name = "UTC")

Construct Whole-Second Instants¶

from_epoch_seconds() interprets each input as an absolute UTC epoch-second count and stores the corresponding nanoseconds. It is appropriate for system interfaces that expose integral seconds and for lossless round trips from epoch_seconds() when every original instant was aligned to a second boundary.

const auto seconds = pluss::make_series({{-1LL, 0LL}, {1LL, pluss::Timeline::kNaT}});
const auto times = pluss::Timeline::from_epoch_seconds(
    seconds, "America/New_York");

std::cout << pluss::series::print(times.epoch_nanos()) << '\n'
          << "shape=[" << times.sizes()[0] << ',' << times.sizes()[1]
          << "], tz=" << times.tz() << '\n';

Output¶

Series(shape=[2,2], strides=[2,1], dtype=int64, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=
⎡          -1000000000                    0 ⎤
⎣           1000000000 -9223372036854775808 ⎦
shape=[2,2], tz=America/New_York

The numeric ticks are unchanged by the presentation zone. Shape is preserved, NaT remains NaT, and multiplication overflow throws. Converting a Timeline to whole seconds and back discards its original subsecond remainder.
